No answer leak detected. The problem asks to determine Lipschitz continuity of the solution with respect to the initial condition — a standard ODE well-posedness question with no embedded solution.

## Proof

**Claim.** The solution $z_{(t_0,x_0)}$ is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the initial condition $x_0$. Specifically, for any $x_0, y_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ and any $t \in [0,T]$,
$$\bigl|z_{(t_0,x_0)}(t) - z_{(t_0,y_0)}(t)\bigr| \le e^{\|L\|_{L^\infty(0,T)}\,T}\,|x_0 - y_0|,$$
where $L(s) := \bigl\|\partial_x f(s,\cdot)\bigr\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R})}$.

---

**Setup.** Since $f \in L^\infty\bigl((0,T);\,W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R})\bigr)$, for a.e. $s \in (0,T)$ the map $x \mapsto f(s,x)$ is globally Lipschitz with constant
$$L(s) := \bigl\|\partial_x f(s,\cdot)\bigr\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R})}, \qquad L \in L^\infty(0,T).$$
The Carathéodory conditions guarantee existence and uniqueness of the global (Carathéodory) solution for every $(t_0,x_0) \in [0,T]\times\mathbb{R}$.

**Step 1 — Difference estimate.** Fix $t_0 \in [0,T]$ and $x_0, y_0 \in \mathbb{R}$. Let $u := z_{(t_0,x_0)}$ and $v := z_{(t_0,y_0)}$. Both satisfy the integral equation, so for $t \ge t_0$:
$$u(t) - v(t) = x_0 - y_0 + \int_{t_0}^{t}\bigl[f(s,u(s)) - f(s,v(s))\bigr]\,\mathrm{d}s.$$
(The case $t \le t_0$ is handled identically with the integral oriented accordingly.) Taking absolute values and using the Lipschitz property of $f(s,\cdot)$ for a.e. $s$:
$$\bigl|u(t)-v(t)\bigr| \le |x_0-y_0| + \int_{t_0}^{t} L(s)\,\bigl|u(s)-v(s)\bigr|\,\mathrm{d}s.$$

**Step 2 — Grönwall's inequality.** Define $w(t) := |u(t)-v(t)|$ and $M := \|L\|_{L^\infty(0,T)} < \infty$. The above reads
$$w(t) \le |x_0-y_0| + \int_{t_0}^{t} L(s)\,w(s)\,\mathrm{d}s.$$
Since $L \in L^\infty(0,T) \subset L^1(0,T)$, the hypotheses of Grönwall's inequality (integral form) are satisfied. Applying it yields
$$w(t) \le |x_0-y_0|\,\exp\!\Bigl(\int_{t_0}^{t} L(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\Bigr) \le |x_0-y_0|\,e^{M\,T}.$$

**Step 3 — Conclusion.** The bound
$$\bigl|z_{(t_0,x_0)}(t) - z_{(t_0,y_0)}(t)\bigr| \le e^{M\,T}\,|x_0 - y_0|, \qquad \forall\, t\in[0,T],$$
holds with the constant $C := e^{\|L\|_{L^\infty(0,T)}\,T}$ depending only on $f$ (through $\|\partial_x f\|_{L^\infty((0,T)\times\mathbb{R})}$) and $T$, and **independent of** $t_0, x_0, y_0$. Therefore the solution map
$$x_0 \;\longmapsto\; z_{(t_0,x_0)}(\cdot) \in C\bigl([0,T]\bigr)$$
is globally Lipschitz continuous (with respect to $x_0$), uniformly in $t \in [0,T]$ and in $t_0 \in [0,T]$.

The essential ingredients are: (i) $W^{1,\infty}$ regularity of $f$ in the state variable provides a uniform-in-time Lipschitz constant $L(s)$; (ii) $L^\infty(0,T) \subset L^1(0,T)$ makes Grönwall applicable with a finite exponential factor; (iii) the Carathéodory conditions ensure both solutions exist globally so the difference is well-defined on all of $[0,T]$. $\blacksquare$
